title: Add scoped-token + request-nonce support; tighten CORS and fix streaming/function-calls for OpenAI-compat layer
author: Elliot Park
description: Context: customer integrations and the OpenAI compatibility shim required clearer auth semantics for project-scoped and org-level keys plus a small but critical request signing nonce header to mitigate replay risks. This PR implements scoped-token handling in the API gateway and the OpenAI-compat adapter, tightens CORS to avoid permissive origins for compatibility endpoints, and fixes two streaming/function-calling regressions observed in the compat layer. Summary of changes: 1) auth: add scoped token parsing and enforcement (project:read, project:invoke) and a transparent project-id header passthrough for private deployments; 2) request signing: introduce X-Redwood-Request-Nonce header and validation hooks used by private on-prem request signers; 3) CORS: restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin for /v1/compat/* routes to configured trusted origins and add preflight caching; 4) OpenAI compatibility: fix chunking logic in streaming adapter to flush partial function-call frames correctly and ensure structured output choices include function_call metadata; 5) SDKs/docs: TypeScript SDK updated to include getScopedToken helper and the compat docs show examples for project-scoped keys and nonce usage. Motivation: several enterprise customers required scoped key semantics to enforce per-project rate limits and audit boundaries; a recent support incident revealed that replayed signed requests could be used to replay function-invocation flows in private deployments. This change is incremental and backwards-compatible for standard API keys (no mandatory token format change). Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests added for scoped-token parsing; [x] e2e openai-compat test covering streaming function call frames; [x] updated docs and quickstart example for scoped tokens; [x] security review comments addressed. Backcompat notes: default behavior is unchanged for existing keys; operators who enable strict nonce validation must deploy signing helper changes to clients. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and operator flags.

refactor(cors): restrict compat endpoints and add preflight cache control

release_notes: Added support for project-scoped tokens. Operators can use scoped tokens to limit keys to specific projects and permissions.
Introduced X-Redwood-Request-Nonce header and server-side validation hooks to reduce replay risk for signed requests (opt-in for existing deployments).
OpenAI compatibility layer: streaming adapter now correctly emits partial function_call frames and preserves structured output metadata.
CORS: compat endpoints are now restricted by default; admins should add trusted origins to the console or chart values.
TypeScript SDK: new getScopedToken helper and example usage for compat endpoints.
